title: E2E specs import the routes' own view types: tsc catches payload drift CI hid

Shares e2e/journey-role-to-schedule.spec.ts and e2e/token-doors-axe.spec.ts with this context's slot-B card (disjoint hunks: wire reads vs the axe helper) - if both are built, build sequentially. body:
## Summary
The e2e suite re-declares every API payload it reads as an inline cast (60 of them), so when a route's projection changes the specs keep compiling and fail - or worse, silently match nothing - only in the CI e2e job. Give the suite one typed reader module whose types are the product's own view types (`import type`), lift the one projection that is trapped in a route file, and let `tsc` - which builders CAN run - catch payload drift at edit time.

## Description
`e2e/wire.ts` exports small typed readers (`readBoard`, `readEntry`, `readSchedule`, `readPublicInvite`, `readDecisionRecords`, `readTask`, `readLifecycles`) over Playwright's `APIRequestContext`, typed from `PipelineEntryView`/`PipelineEntry` (db/pipeline.ts), `ScheduleInvite` (schedule-store.ts), `TaskRecord` (db/tasks.ts), `LifecycleRecord` (db/devcase.ts), `DecisionRecord` + the `verifyDecisionChain` return type (decision-record-store.ts), with stage literals typed as `PipelineStage`. All app imports are `import type`, so nothing server-side loads in Playwright's process. `publicInviteView` moves from `app/api/schedule/[token]/route.ts` into `app/_lib/schedule-public-view.ts` with an exported `PublicInviteView` type and a PUBLIC_INVITE_FIELDS list; the route and the candidate hook (`use-schedule-invite.ts`) both consume it, which also closes the hook's missing `proposals` field. `e2e/wire.typecheck.ts` holds `@ts-expect-error` pins for the facts the journeys depend on (devcase ids are NOT on the board projection; stages are the closed vocabulary). A source-pin test ratchets inline casts in the migrated specs to zero and caps the rest.

## Flow
1. Write app/_lib/schedule-public-view.test.ts and app/e2e-wire-contract.test.ts (red).
2. Lift publicInviteView + PublicInviteView; route and hook import it (wire bytes unchanged).
3. Add e2e/wire.ts readers with describeWireFailure; add e2e/wire.typecheck.ts pins.
4. Migrate journey-one-thread (drop local BoardEntry), journey-role-to-schedule, token-doors-axe, quality-tables onto the readers.
5. Update docs/development/testing-and-evaluation.md (the wire rule) and docs/features/scheduling/README.md (the projection's new home).
6. Gates: tsc, lint, test:unit, docs:check. e2e run owed on the keyless CI job (behaviour-neutral by construction: same calls, same assertions).

## Expected impact
The class that journey-one-thread.spec.ts:345-355 documents - a projection change that turns an e2e assertion into a silent empty match, discovered only in the CI browser job - becomes a `tsc` error at the edit that caused it. The candidate schedule page and the e2e suite stop keeping two hand copies of the public invite wire, and the public projection gets a unit-pinned field allowlist (today it is pinned only by prose).

## Evaluation
Claim: e2e payload reads are compile-checked against the product's own view types and the public invite projection is a shared, pinned module.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass.
After: 8 of 8.
Method: contract - `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` (the @ts-expect-error pins) + `npm run test:unit -- app/_lib/schedule-public-view.test.ts app/e2e-wire-contract.test.ts`; keyless e2e job owed on CI.
Result: pending build.
Gate: contract

title: One axe policy for every spec: a contrast-measured holdout ledger that expires
acceptance: unit: `holdoutVerdict(ledger['eyebrow-coral-on-paper'])` measures contrastRatio(CORAL, PAPER) from app/_lib/brand.ts via app/_lib/brand-config.ts contrastRatio -> 3.66 against bar 4.5 -> `{ stillNeeded: true }`; the same entry evaluated with fg '#a8402f' -> `{ stillNeeded: false }` and a message naming the holdout id to delete

unit: the 'white-label-on-coral' entry (WHITE on CORAL, 3.87 vs 4.5) carries `blocksKeyless: 'token-doors-axe'`; when it evaluates as no longer needed, the message names enrolling token-doors-axe in KEYLESS_SPECS - the promise playwright.config.ts:75-81 makes in prose

unit: every ledger entry has a rule id, a scope (page path or band selector), a non-empty reason, and EITHER a measured token pair OR `artDirection: true` naming a file under app/landing/; an entry with neither fails the test

unit (pure `filterSerious(violations, scope, ledger)` over axe-shaped fixtures): a `color-contrast` violation on a `.text-coral` node in a scope that holds the eyebrow holdout is tolerated, while a `button-name` violation on the SAME node is reported - the case the current `.exclude(".text-coral")` silently hides

unit (pure `unusedHoldouts(ledger, seen, scope)`): a holdout scoped to '/trust' that matched no violation in that page's run is returned as stale - public-pages.spec.ts's shrink-only 'still needed?' rule generalised to every spec

unit (source pin): no `new AxeBuilder(` outside e2e/a11y.ts, no `.exclude(` in any e2e/*.spec.ts, and AXE_TAGS is exactly ["wcag2a","wcag2aa","wcag21a","wcag21aa"] - candidate token doors are held to the bar the marketing pages already meet

unit (source pin): scripts/run-unit-tests.mjs DEFAULT_PATTERNS contains "e2e/**/*.test.ts" and playwright.config.ts declares a testMatch limited to *.spec.ts, so e2e/a11y-policy.test.ts runs under node:test and is NOT also collected by Playwright (whose default testMatch includes *.test.ts)

e2e run OWED on the keyless CI job (builders cannot boot Next): the migrated specs stay green, and any new wcag21 finding on /schedule or /offer lands as a measured ledger entry - never as a dropped tag
premise: ONE token pairing - coral #d65a4a on paper #fdf8ee, 3.66:1 - is handled four different ways: a blanket DOM exclusion `.exclude(".text-coral")` in journey-role-to-schedule.spec.ts:84 and token-doors-axe.spec.ts:110 (hides EVERY rule on those nodes, never expires); a per-page rule holdout asserted to still fail in public-pages.spec.ts:51-56; a per-band holdout in landing.spec.ts:39 (#voice is the same pairing, landing.spec.ts:29); and a whole spec kept out of the release gate in playwright.config.ts:75-81 ('It joins this list when the token is darkened')

The expiry of the exclusion is prose only: journey-role-to-schedule.spec.ts:79-80 'If the design system ever darkens light-theme coral, delete this exclusion' and token-doors-axe.spec.ts:108 repeats it - nothing checks it, and the specs are only run in CI

Five AxeBuilder call sites with three tag sets: analyze-smoke.spec.ts:64-65 and journey-role-to-schedule.spec.ts:82-83 and token-doors-axe.spec.ts:110 use [wcag2a, wcag2aa]; landing.spec.ts:45 and public-pages.spec.ts:61 add wcag21a/wcag21aa - so the candidate token doors (schedule, offer, erasure, invite) are held to a LOWER bar than the marketing pages

The measurement machinery already exists and is pure: app/_lib/brand-config.ts:106 `export function contrastRatio(hex1, hex2)`, reading app/_lib/brand.ts:31 PAPER '#fdf8ee', :33 CORAL '#d65a4a', :39 WHITE '#ffffff' (lockstep with globals.css enforced by design:check)

No e2e policy module can be unit-tested today: scripts/run-unit-tests.mjs:98-103 DEFAULT_PATTERNS are app/, packages/, edge/, i18n/ only, and playwright.config.ts sets no testMatch (grep testMatch -> none), so a *.test.ts under e2e/ would be collected by Playwright instead
rollback: Reverts cleanly: the three new e2e modules are leaves, each spec's local axe helper is restored from the revert, and the runner-glob and testMatch lines are single-line additions whose removal returns both runners to today's collection.
runner_up: Every spec declares its env needs in a parsed header and the keyless pin fails on an undecided spec (jobseeker-keyless.spec.ts, 82 lines, runs in no job) - close to the open S item 'Enrol jobseeker-keyless in KEYLESS_SPECS', so held back.
dependencies: e2e/landing.spec.ts is also written by r09 spark-about-illustrations ('Walk all nine spotlights in one dialog') - build this card AFTER that card lands, and touch only landing's axe helper and CONTRAST_HOLDOUT_BANDS. Shares e2e/journey-role-to-schedule.spec.ts and e2e/token-doors-axe.spec.ts with this context's slot-A card (disjoint hunks) - build sequentially if both are chosen. playwright.config.ts's KEYLESS_SPECS array is not edited (keyless-e2e-pin.test.mjs parses it); only a testMatch line and the token-doors-axe comment's pointer to the ledger change. body:
## Summary
The suite's accessibility gate is five hand-copied helpers with three WCAG tag sets and four incompatible ways of tolerating the same coral-on-paper contrast debt - one of them a blanket DOM exclusion that hides every other rule on those nodes and never expires. Replace them with one axe runner and one ledger of named, rule-scoped holdouts whose contrast is MEASURED from the brand tokens, so the day the palette changes a unit test - not a CI browser run nobody can make locally - names every holdout to delete and the spec to enrol.

## Description
`e2e/a11y-policy.ts` (pure, node-testable) holds AXE_TAGS (one set, wcag2a/aa + 21a/aa), the HOLDOUTS ledger (id, rule, scope, reason, and either `{ fg, bg, bar }` token names measured through `contrastRatio` or `artDirection: true` for app/landing/), and the pure functions `holdoutVerdict`, `filterSerious` and `unusedHoldouts`. `e2e/a11y.ts` is the only place that constructs `AxeBuilder`; specs call `expectA11y(page, scope)`. The `.exclude(".text-coral")` waivers become rule-scoped entries, so a missing label on an eyebrow is caught again. public-pages' and landing's shrink-only lists move into the ledger with their measured ratios. `scripts/run-unit-tests.mjs` gains `e2e/**/*.test.ts` and `playwright.config.ts` gains `testMatch: "**/*.spec.ts"`, which makes every pure e2e policy module unit-testable from now on.

## Flow
1. Write e2e/a11y-policy.test.ts against fixture axe results (red); add the runner glob + testMatch.
2. Implement a11y-policy.ts and a11y.ts.
3. Migrate analyze-smoke, journey-role-to-schedule, token-doors-axe, public-pages, then (after r09 spark lands) landing.
4. Point the token-doors-axe comment in playwright.config.ts at the ledger entry; update docs/development/testing-and-evaluation.md (one policy, how a holdout is added and how it expires).
5. Gates: tsc, lint, test:unit, test:docs (keyless pin still parses). Keyless e2e run owed on CI.

## Expected impact
Closes the class 'accessibility waiver outlives its reason': the coral decision (owner's palette call) becomes a single measured fact that reports, on change, exactly which exclusions and which gate enrolment it unlocks. Candidate-facing token doors - reached from email on a phone, the most consequential page of each flow - are held to the same WCAG 2.1 bar as the marketing pages. Rule-scoped holdouts restore detection of non-contrast defects on the excluded nodes.

## Evaluation
Claim: every axe check in the suite runs through one policy whose holdouts are named, scoped to a rule, measured from tokens and self-expiring.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass.
After: 8 of 8.
Method: policy-tighten - `npm run test:unit -- e2e/a11y-policy.test.ts` (7 cases) + tsc + lint; case 8 is the keyless e2e job on CI, owed.
Result: pending build.
Gate: policy-tighten
